scope: Primary-source bibliographic identity and abstract-level mechanisms; not independent validation of reported performance or a reproduction.

entries.title: EvidentialRAG: Quantifying and Mitigating Information Conflict in Multi-Source Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Evidential Deep Learning
entries.finding: Primary record identifies ERAG: claim support becomes Dirichlet evidence; conflict-preserving Dempster-Shafer fusion represents unresolved disagreement as uncertainty, which routes answering or abstention.
entries.relevance: Direct comparison for uncertainty-aware conflict handling. Preserving conflicting records in a context is not implementation of evidential fusion or calibrated abstention.

entries.title: ArbGraph: Conflict-Aware Evidence Arbitration for Reliable Long-Form Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entries.finding: Primary abstract describes atomic claims, support/contradiction graph edges, and iterative credibility propagation before generation.
entries.relevance: Direct comparison for pre-generation arbitration; atomic record-group packing does not reproduce claim extraction or graph arbitration.

entries.title: MemFlow: Intent-Driven Memory Orchestration for Small Language Model Agents
entries.finding: Review's bounded-context orchestration description matches this primary record: intent routing, three retrieval/reasoning tiers, tier-dependent context budgets, and optional validation/retry.
entries.relevance: Compare context construction and routing costs on shared tasks. MemFlow is an overloaded name; this identity excludes optical-flow, video-generation and systems-memory projects.

entries.title: Verifiable Memory: Learning Unified Memory Management with Local and Global Verifiers for Large Language Model Agents
entries.finding: VerMem learns a unified memory-operation policy with supervised initialization and reinforcement learning; local transition and global coherence verifiers supply training signals. Verifiers are used only during training.
entries.relevance: Comparison concerns learned memory management and verification. A conflict-aware answer prompt is not the trained VerMem policy or its verifiers.

entries.title: Decoupling Memory from Context: Structured Memory for Token-Efficient Test-Time Continual Learning
entries.finding: This paper explicitly names its system GraphMemory: a graph of reusable strategies retrieved as query-relevant subgraphs under bounded retrieval. Primary record revised 6 October 2026.
entries.relevance: Review's graph-structured bounded-context description matches this system. GraphMemory is not the paper title and should not be silently substituted with a graph-memory survey or G-Memory.

entries.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Conflicting Evidence
entries.finding: RAMDocs (Retrieval with Ambiguity and Misinformation in Documents) is a dataset introduced in this paper, jointly covering ambiguity, misinformation and noise.
entries.relevance: External conflict benchmark candidate. It is not a distinct paper, not evidence of a completed local benchmark, and not a source of assumed bitemporal annotations.

entries.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Conflicting Evidence
entries.finding: MADAM-RAG is the multi-agent debate and response-aggregation method introduced alongside RAMDocs in the same paper.
entries.relevance: Conflict-aware generation comparator requiring its own faithful protocol. A local conflict-aware reader prompt is not a reproduction of MADAM-RAG.

entries.title: EHR-RAG: Bridging Long-Horizon Structured Electronic Health Records and Large Language Models via Enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entries.finding: Primary abstract describes event/time-aware hybrid retrieval, adaptive iterative retrieval, and factual/counterfactual evidence paths for structured longitudinal EHR prediction.
entries.relevance: Cross-domain temporal retrieval comparison. This source does not establish clinical validity or dual valid-time/observation-time semantics for the local selector.

entries.title: MiniLM: Deep Self-Attention Distillation for Task-Agnostic Compression of Pre-Trained Transformers
entries.finding: Foundational self-attention distillation paper, not sufficient identity for sentence-embedding weights. Publisher/maintainer model cards establish the separate encoder provenance below.
entries.relevance: Local dense retrieval uses a pretrained sentence encoder from the MiniLM family. No distillation training or original MiniLM experiments were reproduced here.
entries.implementation_scope: Pretrained encoder inference component only, as inspected in research/advanced_retrieval.py; this audit did not execute inference or validate scores.

model_identity.local_pooling: attention-mask mean followed by L2 normalization
model_identity.naming_note: The sentence encoder's v2 suffix is not evidence that the distinct MiniLMv2 paper is its identity. Base card describes a six-layer model retaining alternate layers from microsoft/MiniLM-L12-H384-uncased.

entries.title: Reciprocal rank fusion outperforms condorcet and individual rank learning methods
entries.finding: Author-affiliated Google Research record verifies title, authors, SIGIR 2009 and pages 758-759; publisher search metadata verifies DOI. Direct ACM page fetch returned HTTP 403.
entries.relevance: Local hybrid ranking adds reciprocal ranks from BM25 and dense lists with k=60 and equal weights; this is an established fusion component, not a new retrieval algorithm.
entries.implementation_scope: rank_texts hybrid branch in research/advanced_retrieval.py: sum(1/(60+rank)), ranks starting at 1. No original SIGIR evaluation was reproduced by this audit.
